summary: Create new world screen appears even when world is created; clicking on button causes freeze or crash
description: The bug I just created a new world to test out the new features, but the game froze for a second after I enabled the 1.20 data pack. When I clicked on continue, nothing happened until the game unfreeze. But the create world button is in the same place as the continue button. So when the world loaded up, I was met with the create new world screen again. When I created a world again, it got stuck on preparing world for creation Steps to reproduce - Create World Tab - Experiments - Double click on Done - Now, you will get two buttons, if you click Create New World game will softlock
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Open the Create New World menu.
4. Navigate to the Experiments section.
5. Double click on Done to enable the 1.20 data pack.
6. Wait approximately 1 second and observe the game freeze momentarily.
7. Click on the Continue button after the freeze ends.
8. Observe that the Create New World screen appears instead of loading the created world.
9. Click on the Create New World button.
10. Observe that the game gets stuck on preparing world for creation.
Observed Behavior: The actual behavior of the game is that after creating a new world to test the features associated with the 1.20 data pack, the game experiences a brief freeze when the data pack is enabled. Upon clicking the continue button, there is no immediate response, and the game only resumes after the freeze ends. However, when the world finally loads, the player is unexpectedly presented with the create new world screen instead of the newly created world. If the player attempts to create a world again, the game becomes stuck on the preparing world for creation stage. To reproduce this issue, one must navigate to the Create World tab, enable the Experiments feature, double-click on Done, and then click the Create New World button, which results in the game softlocking.
Expected Behavior: When following the reproduction steps, the game should successfully load the newly created world without displaying the "Create New World" screen again. Instead of freezing or crashing, clicking the "Continue" button should transition the player directly into the game environment of the created world. The game should not exhibit any softlock behavior, allowing for seamless gameplay and access to the new features without interruption.
